charts.title: cellcell-executable-compete-dynamics
charts.caption: Interactive: competition — the weaker cell starves. cell_a's viability holds at 1.0 the whole run while cell_b's collapses fast, dropping below 0.5 within the first two steps (the dashed line marks competitive exclusion); by t=20, cell_b viability ≈ 0.0001. The shared nutrient pool settles at ≈0.20, measurably depleted — confirming the coupling is real, not two isolated cells. Two cells over one shared nutrient negotiate viability; same coupling interface, one handler env with asymmetric vmax (Law 4).

charts.title: cellcell-executable-crossfeed-dynamics
charts.caption: Interactive: cross-feeding — both persist. Over the same coupling interface, only the handler swapped for a symmetric vmax with byproduct return, both cell_a and cell_b viability stay at 1.0 the whole run and the shared nutrient pool settles higher (≈0.54) because the returned byproduct offsets combined uptake. Two cells over one shared nutrient negotiate viability; same coupling interface, a different handler env (Law 4).
